description: Survival needs: hunger, thirst, temperature and sleep (P9c.core; catalog survival-needs; src/survival/needs.ts). Stamina is not a need here (stamina.json). Ops: tuning {survival?: SurvivalIR, params?} -> SurvivalTuning (per field over Babylon's defaults; params are the pack's flat parameters); initial {survival?, params?, at?} -> SurvivalState; run {survival?, params?, start, steps: [{do: advance (at) | restore (need, amount, at) | action (action, amount?, at) | consume (effects, at) | use_item (item {type, quantity?, effects?}, at) | set_temperature (value, at) | modifier (preset | modifier, at) | remove_modifier (id) | enable (enabled) | save (at)}]} -> each step's result (a refused step: {do, ok: false, reason}); save {state, at} -> the block; load {survival?, params?, block, at} -> SurvivalState, refusal unreadable_survival (block) with keys. Time runs in whole ticks of tickMs (default 1000), the remainder kept; each tick expires modifiers (T - startedAt >= duration > 0), decays each need by decayRate x the product of its modifiers x tickMs/1000 floored at 0 (environment-driven temperature drifts toward its target by temperatureDriftPerSecond x tickMs/1000 instead), re-reads its band (critical <= criticalThreshold, else warning <= warningThreshold; temperature with criticalAtBothExtremes also at >= max - threshold) raising need_critical / need_warning / need_restored on a change, and charges a deprived need (temperature: critical; others: 0) damageRate x globalDamageMultiplier x tickMs/1000 into damageOwed; each advance hands the whole points over as hurt. A restore ending at >= satisfiedFraction x max raises need_satisfied. use_item spends one of a consumable, food or drink stack (consumed 1, remaining quantity - 1; a missing quantity reads 1) and restores its effects, or, when they name no tracked need, performs eat (food) or drink (drink); collectible, document, key and quest items are used unspent (consumed 0); another type is refused not_usable, a stack under 1 not_held. A performed action restores its restoreActions row once at its flat amount (sleep: Rest 50 per sleep). Every number is rounded to 4 places after each operation. Runner: src/survival/systems-corpus.ts. Every case {name, op, input, expected}; compare exactly, object key sets included; an unknown op or step is an error, never a skip. Regenerate with npm run survival-corpus; npm run survival-corpus:check fails on any difference. See docs/survival-systems.md.

rules.restoreActions: The restore-actions hook is an action id: a performed action whose id is a restoreActions key restores that row once, at its flat amount (eat: hunger 30, drink: thirst 25, sleep: Rest 50; Godot survival_system.gd). sleep is the action matrix's Sleep (event furniture_slept, the bed's verb in the original game), and restores 50 per sleep whatever its length, as Godot's sleep_rest ignored its duration.
rules.itemUse: Using an item (useItemForNeeds): a consumable, food or drink item spends one of its stack and restores the needs its effects name; when they name no tracked need, food performs eat and drink performs drink (Godot eat(item_id, 30) / drink(item_id, 25) took the item); a consumable restores nothing then. A collectible, document, key or quest item is used unspent (the original game's handleUseItem). Another type is refused not_usable; a stack under 1 not_held.
rules.stack: One of a stack, never the whole has_item/3 fact: the original game's handleUseItem called inventory.removeItem(item.id, 1), InventoryModel.removeItem takes 1 by default, and the use_item and consume action effects (prolog/action-effects.ts TAKE_ONE_ITEM_EFFECT) now replace has_item(A, I, N) with N - 1, dropping it at 0.

openQuestions: Which prop or verb performs Sleep in a world (needs_ruling, core's owner or the catalog owner): core has no bed interactable; the original game's beds (Babylon FurnitureInteractionManager) slept only from 20:00 to 05:00 and advanced the clock to 07:00. Until that is ruled, a host binds Sleep to whatever verb it already offers for the action matrix's sleep, or to none.
Whether a sleep also refills stamina (needs_ruling): Godot's sleep_rest restored stamina 30 as well; core's stamina is the pool, recovered by rest ticks, and the sleep row restores Rest only.

Whether an item's energy effect (Babylon: effects.energy, or +15 for any consumable with no effects) restores the stamina pool (needs_ruling, the stamina pack's owner): useItemForNeeds reads only the four needs.

A need climbing from critical to warning still raises need_warning ("<Need> is getting low"), as Godot did; the stamina bar no longer does (hud.json). Whether the needs take the same climb rule is open.

cases.name: tuning: no survival section is the four default needs (Babylon's numbers); stamina is not one of them
tuning: only the authored needs, in the IR's order; a stamina row and an unknown id are ignored; a missing field falls back to that need's default, a start above max clamps
tuning: an empty needs list tracks none; pack parameters override flat fields; a mistyped parameter is ignored; tickMs floors and is at least 1
tuning: a fractional tickMs and maxTicksPerAdvance floor to whole numbers
initial: each need at its start value, the clock at the given time
initial: a need that starts in a band starts there, with no event (hunger warning; temperature critical at the hot extreme)
run: needs decay per whole tick of 1000 ms; a part tick waits for the next call
run: sixty seconds in one call
run: the same sixty seconds in four uneven calls reach the same readings
run: into warning, then critical, then empty: each band change raises its event once; at zero hunger hurts 2 a tick
run: damage accrues per tick; whole points go to hurt and the fraction stays owed
run: globalDamageMultiplier scales every need's damage
run: a long advance raises one damage_from_need per need, at the first tick it was charged, carrying the whole call's damage
run: need_satisfied at exactly satisfiedFraction x max, not just below it
run: damage disabled: a need at zero hurts nothing
run: eat, drink and sleep add Godot's amounts and clamp at max; leaving warning raises need_restored; ending at 90% or more raises need_satisfied, a drain never does; a negative amount drains
run: refusals change nothing: an unknown action, a need the world does not track (stamina), an amount that is not a number
run: a critical need restored into warning raises need_warning, not need_restored
run: consuming an item restores each tracked need its effects name, in tuning order; other keys are ignored
run: a preset modifier halves hunger's decay; the same id refreshes it; it expires at its duration, before that tick's decay
run: two modifiers multiply; a permanent one never expires; removing it restores the base rate; unknown and untracked modifiers are refused
run: environment-driven temperature drifts 10 a second toward its target; cold reaches warning then critical and hurts; warmth restores it
run: environment-driven with criticalAtBothExtremes off: only the cold end is a band, and a critical temperature hurts before it reaches 0 (Godot)
run: environment-driven heat climbs toward max: warning, then critical at the hot extreme, and it hurts there too
run: environment targets between the comfort zone and the extremes are proportional; a reading within one step lands on the target
run: not environment-driven, set_temperature sets the reading at once (Babylon), clamped; both extremes are critical
run: criticalAtBothExtremes off: only the cold end is a band, and temperature hurts only at zero
run: disabled, ticks pass and nothing decays; enabled again, decay resumes at the next whole tick
run: a clock that goes backwards runs no tick
run: more ticks than maxTicksPerAdvance: the rest are skipped and reported, not queued
run: a save mid-run keeps the readings and each modifier's remaining time
save: readings by id; a timed modifier keeps its remaining ms (never below 0), a permanent one null
load: readings clamp into [0, max]; a missing one starts at its start value; bands re-read with no event; modifiers rebased on the load's clock, spent and untracked ones dropped
load: no block is a new playthrough
load: an unreadable block is refused, naming each unreadable member in order
load: a block that is not an object is refused with no member named
load: a negative rateMultiplier is unreadable, like any other bad modifier row
load: a repeated modifier id keeps its first row and drops the rest
run: using food spends one of its stack (not the whole has_item fact) and restores the needs its effects name; the last one empties the stack
run: food or drink whose effects name no tracked need performs eat or drink at the restoreActions amount (Godot eat 30, drink 25); a consumable restores nothing then
run: a document, key, quest or collectible item is used without being spent; another type is refused (not_usable), as is a stack holding none (not_held)
run: food in a world that does not track hunger is still spent, one of the stack, and restores nothing
run: the restore-actions hook is an action id: sleep (the action matrix's Sleep, the bed's verb) restores Rest by its flat 50 per sleep, whatever its length; eat and drink by id the same way
